name: Take Off Your Pants and Jacket

podcast.body: Released on June 12th, 2001, this album was created under pressure from their record label to deliver another pop punk hit, leading to creative tensions within the band. It was slightly heavier than "Enema of the State" and became the first punk record to debut at number one on the American album charts, selling around 15 million copies. The album's success was pivotal in the growth of pop punk and pop emo in the early 2000s. "It became the first punk record to debut at number one on the American album charts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 2001, this album solidified Blink-182's leading position in the 21st-century pop punk scene, selling an additional 50 million copies. "Blink 182 was way out in front, especially after the 2001 album Take Off Your Pants and Jacket, which by the way sold another 50 million copies."
